summary: The main article describes a visible-light/nickel-catalyzed carboxylation of (hetero)aryl and vinyl bromides using sodium formate as a CO2 source. The document includes a comparison of catalytic strategies, an optimization table for HAT catalysts, an evaluation of sulfonylating agents, and a substrate scope table.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Catalytic strategies for C(sp 2 ) carboxylation.
items.description: Comparison of previous carboxylation methods using CO2 or electrochemical processes with the current work's formate activation strategy.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions for the carboxylation of 3-bromoanisole.
items.description: Screening of various HAT catalysts, identifying phenyl triflimide as the most effective additive for the carboxylation of electron-neutral arenes.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Evaluation of alternative sulfonylating agents in place of phenyl triflimide.
items.description: Comparison of yields using methanesulfonyl chloride and toluenesulfonyl chloride against phenyl triflimide.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Scope of Ni/Photoredox-Catalyzed Carboxylation of (Hetero)Aryl Bromides and Sodium Formate
items.description: Substrate scope showing the carboxylation of various aryl, heteroaryl, and vinyl bromides with functional group tolerance.
